newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Most Brazil congressmen support re-election.
newsitem.headline: Most Brazil congressmen support re-election.

text.p: An overwhelming majority of Brazilian congressmen support the idea of re-election, but not for current president Fernando Henrique Cardoso, a survey published on Sunday showed.

The Datafolha poll carried by the Folha de Sao Paulo newspaper found 77 percent of parliamentarians questioned would back a constitutional amendment allowing sitting presidents, governors and mayors to seek a second consecutive term.
But only 39 percent of those thought the right to stand again should be granted to the incumbent.
Datafolha questioned 434 deputies and 68 senators, 84 percent of Congress, the newspaper said.

In the past month, the issue of re-election has taken centre stage in Brasilia, with Cardoso keen to ensure continuity of his two-year-old "Plano Real" economic stabilisation plan which has beaten hyperinflation down to about 20 percent a year.

If Cardoso wins his bid to change the constitution, he will become the first Brazilian president to be allowed to stand again. Fearing the stigma of past Imperial rule, Brazil has not allowed re-election since the republic was founded in 1889.
Congress was due to set up a special committee to start discussing the proposal on around Oct. 23.
The Datafolha survey, carried out between Oct. 10-17, found 14 percent of congressmen firmly against re-election and nine percent undecided.
